newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: AUSTRALIA YIELD SPREADS-BACK TO OUTPERFORMING WAYS.
newsitem.headline: AUSTRALIA YIELD SPREADS-BACK TO OUTPERFORMING WAYS.

text.p: Australian bonds put in a strong outperformance against the dollar bloc, spurred on by a benign set of final wages data for the second quarter.
The Australian/U.S. 10-year bond yield spread was shrinking back to last week's low of around 25 basis points, having neared 50 basis points on Wednesday.

"To some extent, bond markets still don't believe the good inflation/wage story in Australia. This takes time, and the true test is in a period of stronger growth," said Craig James, senior economist at Colonial State Bank.
"However current and prospective inflationary conditions indicate that a differential of 20-30 basis points on Australian 10-year bond yields over the U.S. is sustainable," he added.

Overall, final wages growth was revised down to 0.3 percent on the quarter, bringing the annual rate down to 3.5 percent from 3.7 percent, while key private sector earnings fell 0.1 percent for an annual rate of 2.5 percent.

The local market had been dogged by fragile U.S. Treasuries in the past week, and although the latter ended firm on Wednesday following PPI and retail sales data, the rally lacked conviction and prices ended well below the day's highs.
The U.S. faces July CPI later on Wednesday.
